data.narrative:
XDOF, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Philipp Wu, Fred Shentu, and Nemo Jin, has raised $142M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of five companies in robotics and manufacturing at same or adjacent stages, supplemented by one public comparable and eight additional private peers including Humanoid, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $142M raised as a valuation proxy, applies a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier to arrive at $284M. Peer-median analysis across the five comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B). The peer set spans from Seed through Series B, with two Series B companies valued at $1.8B and $2.0B, and one Series A peer (Humanoid) at $1.4B.

These methods produce a triangulated range of $241M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $967M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around stage and market positioning relative to the peer cohort. The stage-progression method implies modest upside from raised capital, while peer comparison anchors higher, particularly given the presence of comparable Series A and Series B robotics companies valued at $1.4B–$2.0B. Key sensitivities include peer selection within the robotics manufacturing sector and XDOF's position relative to Series B-stage progression.
